Thunderbirds came in with a 2% below average attack and a 3% leakier than average defense (3-3, 92 scored and 73.3 allowed a game over 6 games), worth about 175 and 180 games of evidence. Projected to score 75.3, they scored 102 (+26.7 points, 35% over); projected to allow 79.4, they allowed 104 (+24.6 points, 31% over).

Red Wolves came in with a 3% below average attack and a league-average defense (3-2, 84.2 scored and 77.4 allowed a game over 5 games), worth about 179 and 179 games of evidence. Projected to score 79.4, they scored 104 (+24.6 points, 31% over); projected to allow 75.3, they allowed 102 (+26.7 points, 35% over).

The bigger miss was Thunderbirds' scoring (+26.7 points against projection); both sides outscored their projections, so the game ran hotter than either team's numbers said.
